title: The Surprisingly Recent History of Peer Review
explainer: Peer review is often traced to the Royal Society's Philosophical Transactions, founded in 1665, but historians of science note the journal ran for over a century without anything resembling a formal referee process; independent written reports from named outside reviewers only became common practice around the 1830s, and most scientific journals did not adopt systematic peer review until well into the 20th century. Knowing that "peer-reviewed" is a newer and less uniform institution than it sounds is a useful caution against treating that label as a quality guarantee rather than one imperfect filter among several — which is exactly why learning to critique a paper's actual methods and evidence still matters.
